ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a benzo six-membered ring structure, with a benzene ring on the left and a partially saturated six-membered ring on the right. The lower ring carbon is connected to an OSO2H sulfate ester group; there is an explicit H at the adjacent upper position; the upper-right carbon is simultaneously connected to OH and NHNHPh. In the figure there is a curved arrow from OH pointing to H+, and another curved arrow indicates migration of adjacent C-H/bond electrons into the ring. Reasoning: According to the arrow pushing, OH and the proton undergo acid-base electron rearrangement; the adjacent C-H bond electrons form a new C=C, making the bond between the carbon bearing NHNHPh and the adjacent ring carbon a double bond. The benzene ring, the phenylhydrazino group NHNHPh, the ring carbon bearing explicit H, and the OSO2H substituent remain on the corresponding skeleton. Thus the organic product can be encoded as [H]C1C(NNc2ccccc2)=CC3=CC=CC=C3C1OS(O)=O, and the separate base fragment [B] is retained, giving the final state.

Keep the benzene ring, phenylhydrazino substituent, explicit H-bearing ring carbon, and sulfate ester unchanged. Encode the organic product as [H]C1C(NNc2ccccc2)=CC3=CC=CC=C3C1OS(O)=O and append the separate base fragment to obtain [H]C1C(NNc2ccccc2)=CC3=CC=CC=C3C1OS(O)=O.[B].
